root_cause.text: The mt76 driver failed to destroy the page_pool and free associated buffers for WED RRO (Receive-Ring-Offload) RX queues during device cleanup, because `mt76_dma_cleanup()` unconditionally skipped those queues when WED was active, and even when WED was inactive, `mt76_dma_rx_cleanup()` did not free the buffers for WED RRO queues (only checked `mt76_queue_is_wed_rro()` and skipped them entirely), causing a memory leak.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The mt76 driver failed to destroy the page_pool and free associated buffers for WED RRO (Receive-Ring-Offload) RX queues during device cleanup, because `mt76_dma_cleanup()` unconditionally skipped those queues when WED was active, and even when WED was inactive, `mt76_dma_rx_cleanup()` did not free the buffers for WED RRO queues (only checked `mt76_queue_is_wed_rro()` and skipped them entirely), causing a memory leak.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix buffer cleanup to not release page pool buffers that belong to active WED RRO queues and related queues, preventing memory corruption.
intent_record.what: In mt76_dma_rx_cleanup, the condition for calling mt76_put_page_pool_buf is changed: first, if the queue is WED_RRO and WED is active, the loop continues (skips freeing); then, the put is only called if the queue is not WED_RRO_RXDMAD_C and not WED_RRO_IND. Previously, the put was called for any queue that was not WED_RRO.
intent_record.how: This change prevents freeing buffers for queue types that are handled by WED hardware (WED_RRO, WED_RRO_RXDMAD_C, WED_RRO_IND) when appropriate, avoiding potential double-free or use-after-free issues. For WED_RRO, the skip is conditional on WED being active; for the other two types, the skip is unconditional.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure proper cleanup of NAPI and DMA resources for all RX queues, including WED RRO queues, to prevent resource leaks.
intent_record.what: Removed an if-statement condition that skipped netif_napi_del and mt76_dma_rx_cleanup for RX queues when the WED device is active and the queue is a WED RRO queue.
intent_record.how: During mt76_dma_cleanup, all RX queues will now unconditionally call netif_napi_del and mt76_dma_rx_cleanup, whereas previously some queues (WED RRO) were skipped if WED was active.

grouping_result.intent: Fix buffer cleanup to not release page pool buffers that belong to active WED RRO queues and related queues, preventing memory corruption.
Ensure proper cleanup of NAPI and DMA resources for all RX queues, including WED RRO queues, to prevent resource leaks.

relevance_review.reason: The group's intent is to avoid releasing page pool buffers that belong to active WED RRO queues to prevent memory corruption, whereas the vulnerability root cause is about failing to free those buffers entirely, leading to a memory leak. The group does not address the leak; it adds a condition that would preserve the skipping behavior, which is opposite to fixing the leak.

The group's core intent is to fix the cleanup of NAPI and DMA resources for all RX queues, specifically including WED RRO queues, which directly addresses the vulnerability root cause of the memory leak due to improper cleanup.

This check identifies WED RRO queues; when combined with WED active, it causes the loop to skip cleaning up those queues, resulting in resource leaks.
This statement directly skips NAPI deletion and DMA cleanup for WED RRO queues when WED is active, preventing proper resource release.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement directly skips NAPI deletion, page_pool destroy, and buffer free for WED RRO RX queues when WED is active, causing a memory leak by preventing proper resource release.
This condition checks if WED is active; when true, it causes the loop to skip cleanup of WED RRO queues, leading to incomplete cleanup and memory leak.
This check identifies WED RRO queues; combined with the WED active condition, it causes the loop to skip cleanup for those queues, preventing buffer and resource deallocation.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows that in mt76_dma_cleanup() (line 1060-1064), a check is added to skip cleanup for WED RRO queues when WED is active: 'if (mtk_wed_device_active(&dev->mmio.wed) && mt76_queue_is_wed_rro(q)) continue;'. This causes the page_pool and buffers to not be freed. Additionally, in mt76_dma_rx_cleanup() (line 822), the code skips freeing buffers for WED RRO queues: 'if (!mt76_queue_is_wed_rro(q)) mt76_put_page_pool_buf(buf, false);'. These changes introduce the memory leak vulnerability described in the root cause.
